title: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide for sarcoma
indication: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
purpose: Your team may choose a combination when reducing tumour size is an important goal and you are fit for more intensive treatment. For advanced disease, treatment generally aims at control and symptom relief; a combination is not a guarantee of longer survival.
schedule: NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 20 mg/m² and ifosfamide 3000 mg/m² on each of days 1–3, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Per-cycle totals are doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9000 mg/m². Mesna, hydration and other support continue for their prescribed periods.
admin: Each treatment day includes intravenous doxorubicin followed by a 3-hour ifosfamide infusion, with prescribed mesna and fluids. Mesna includes a prolonged infusion and hydration continues after chemotherapy; the service confirms admission, pump arrangements and the actual finish time.
scope: This is NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9 g/m² per cycle. The two NCCP combination regimens have different doxorubicin doses and eligibility details. They must not be substituted for each other or for a published 10 g/m² ifosfamide regimen.
consent: Discuss the treatment goal, alternatives including supportive care, uncertainty of benefit, common and serious risks, lasting effects and individual priorities. Record questions and the agreed plan. This is NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9 g/m² per cycle. The two NCCP combination regimens have different doxorubicin doses and eligibility details. They must not be substituted for each other or for a published 10 g/m² ifosfamide regimen.
generic: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste change, diarrhoea or constipation; tiredness, hair and skin changes; infusion reactions and intravenous-line complications; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. Risks differ between medicines and people. The medicine-specific section explains the main additional risks for this regimen.

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA and interferes with repair
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care.
agents.watch: Report breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations or ankle swelling promptly. Tell the nurse immediately about pain or burning at the infusion site. Red urine can occur briefly after the dose; painful urination, clots or persistent redness need assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth ulcers, hair loss and fatigue
Heart muscle damage or rhythm problems; heart damage may appear later and can be permanent
Severe tissue injury if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Fertility and pregnancy harm; rare later leukaemia or other blood cancers

agents.name: Ifosfamide
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA needed for cell division
agents.explanation: Ifosfamide damages cancer-cell DNA. Its breakdown products can also affect the bladder, kidneys and brain. Mesna protects the bladder but does not prevent all kidney or brain effects.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Bladder inflammation or bleeding; kidney damage and electrolyte loss, sometimes lasting
Brain effects causing confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations or seizures
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness, hair loss and fatigue
Fertility and pregnancy harm; rare serious heart or lung injury and later cancers
agents.watch: Report confusion, sleepiness, blood in urine or reduced urine immediately.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm the full three-day treatment and post-treatment mesna/fluid plan, G-CSF injections, stomach protection and anti-sickness medicines before starting. Tell the team about sedating medicines or new confusion. Do not change fluid intake or medicines without the team’s advice. Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential bladder protection. NCCP requires G-CSF support and proton-pump inhibitor prophylaxis for this regimen; the team specifies product, dose and timing. Multi-day anti-sickness treatment needs a single reconciled prescription. Aprepitant may increase ifosfamide-related brain toxicity, so pharmacy must check the chosen plan.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or PICC, agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements. Confirm who manages the mesna pump and when it is disconnected; do not alter pump settings yourself.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding as directed. Your team must give written contraception and post-treatment precautions for every medicine, using current product information; the required duration may differ by medicine and between patients.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment, fitness and your priorities. Surgery and radiotherapy may help local control in selected circumstances; their role and timing are decided separately. Chemotherapy does not automatically replace an operation or radiotherapy. Supportive and palliative care can be used alongside cancer treatment to help symptoms and daily life.

monitoring.title: Tests and care through treatment

rows.label: Safety tests and symptoms
cells: Complete baseline checks in the full treatment reference.
Repeat cycle tests and the regimen-specific checks in your written test plan.
Report symptoms promptly; extra tests may be needed.
Follow abnormal results and lasting effects until a plan is agreed.

rows.label: Medicines and practical care
cells: Confirm the written treatment and support prescriptions.
Record actual treatment, support and any safety hold.
Follow the support and contact plan.
Review ongoing support and line-care or removal needs.

rows.label: Cancer treatment and follow-up
cells: Agree the treatment goal and baseline cancer assessment.
Review benefit using the specialist plan.
Report new or changing cancer-related symptoms.
Agree the next sarcoma treatment or follow-up plan.

monitoring.note: Safety testing and cancer-response assessment have different purposes. Your plan may change after illness or a dose adjustment.

tests.label: Full blood count
tests.purpose: Check white cells for infection risk, haemoglobin for anaemia and platelets for bleeding risk.
tests.timing: Before first treatment and before each cycle. Extra counts may be needed for symptoms or abnormal results.

tests.label: Kidney and liver tests
tests.purpose: Check safe medicine handling and identify kidney or liver effects.
tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner for symptoms, abnormal results or clinical concerns.

tests.label: Heart assessment and lifetime exposure
tests.purpose: Assess anthracycline-related heart risk and account for previous doxorubicin or related treatment.
tests.timing: ECG before treatment. ECHO or MUGA if over 65 or clinically indicated; the source baseline LVEF criterion is above 50%. Review cardiac symptoms and cumulative anthracycline exposure during treatment; further heart tests follow clinical risk or symptoms.

tests.label: Neurological checks
tests.timing: Before each ifosfamide dose; assess immediately for new confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations or seizures.

tests.label: Urine, fluid balance and electrolytes
tests.purpose: Detect bladder bleeding, kidney injury or fluid/electrolyte problems despite mesna.
tests.timing: Check for blood in urine before each ifosfamide dose and every 8 hours on treatment days. Urine output, fluid balance and electrolytes follow the individual ifosfamide and hydration prescription.

tests.label: Medicines and symptoms
tests.purpose: Check interactions, treatment toxicity and whether support prescriptions are complete.
tests.timing: Before treatment and at each treatment review; report new symptoms or medicine changes between visits.

tests.label: Cancer response and follow-up
tests.purpose: Assess cancer control separately from safety blood tests.
tests.timing: Your consultant sets the scan and clinical-review schedule according to the sarcoma and treatment aim.

evidence.title: EORTC 62012: doxorubicin with or without intensified ifosfamide
evidence.summary: In a first-line advanced soft tissue sarcoma trial, adding intensified ifosfamide increased tumour response and delayed progression, but did not demonstrate a statistically significant overall-survival advantage and caused substantially more toxicity. This helps explain why a combination may be considered when tumour shrinkage is especially important.
evidence.intro: In a first-line advanced soft tissue sarcoma trial, adding intensified ifosfamide increased tumour response and delayed progression, but did not demonstrate a statistically significant overall-survival advantage and caused substantially more toxicity. This helps explain why a combination may be considered when tumour shrinkage is especially important.
evidence.caveat: The trial used doxorubicin 75 mg/m² with ifosfamide 10 g/m² over four days. NCCP 00391 uses doxorubicin 60 mg/m² with ifosfamide 9 g/m² over three days. Trial response or survival figures are not validated estimates for this exact schedule. The advanced-disease trial does not establish neoadjuvant benefit.
evidence.interpretation: The trial used doxorubicin 75 mg/m² with ifosfamide 10 g/m² over four days. NCCP 00391 uses doxorubicin 60 mg/m² with ifosfamide 9 g/m² over three days. Trial response or survival figures are not validated estimates for this exact schedule. The advanced-disease trial does not establish neoadjuvant benefit.
